# Open questions and future directions {#sec-open}

This chapter separates what is unresolved, what the evidence cannot yet support, and what has been proposed but not done.
Nothing in the third group should be read as a result.

## What we do not yet know

**The central question.** [Two different kinds of information may resolve the split: knowledge of calcification and the sum, which makes the exchange visible to the data, and a prior that is not symmetric between the two tissues, such as a small amount of weak supervision; which is more plausible is a hypothesis to be tested by the staged plan.]{#clm-0049 .claim}
The pilot supplied the sum from the truth, so it leaves open whether the spatially varying fat/gland error can be recovered
without that knowledge, and whether any of it carries over to a trained network (@sec-information). [It is also undecided whether
the large high-frequency adipose error seen in the pilot reflects a real failure to recover spatial structure or only
out-of-range excursions near calcifications, because the clipped, away-from-lesion version of the metric has not been run.]{#clm-0132 .claim}
[The pilot's own positive control (starts perturbed from the truth should converge and recover) failed on all three cases, so its
non-recoveries are control or solver failures until shown otherwise rather than evidence about identifiability.]{#clm-0143 .claim}

**The one unexplained success.** [One label-free run (one seed of one output form) reached a material error of 0.091 with
correct anatomy while its siblings did not, and its mechanism is unknown; a success rate cannot be estimated from one in three
seeds.]{#clm-0133 .claim} It is a lead, not a method (@sec-labelfree).

**Detector realism.** [Realistic photon-counting detector effects (energy response, charge sharing, pile-up, calibration)
may change identifiability and model mismatch relative to the idealised bins studied so far.]{#clm-0046 .claim} The
idealised comparison in @sec-mismatch should not be used to argue for or against a detector.

**Mismatch in learned maps.** [Training on one forward model and testing on a mismatched one (no inverse crime) has not been done: only forward-model projection differences (2-3%) and toy-model estimator bias have been measured.]{#clm-0050 .claim} The projection comparison used an independent simulator on disk phantoms (@sec-trust); supervised and self-supervised studies on its data are proposed, not run.

**Generalisation.** [Whether models trained on procedural phantoms generalise to unseen material compositions is not yet
tested.]{#clm-0048 .claim}

**Transfer.** [Whether material fields learned from simulated pairs transfer to real or clinical spectral CT, and how this
could be measured without clinical truth, is not yet studied.]{#clm-0047 .claim}

## Gaps in the evidence

- [The held-out test split of 100 cases has never been evaluated; every learned number is on the validation split.]{#clm-0134 .claim}
- [Most learned results use three seeds or fewer, and the prior and refinement experiments one seed per setting; with the
  baseline seed range of about 0.017 in material error, differences below roughly 0.03 to 0.035 would be hard to detect with
  three seeds, and for the most variable output form (seed range 0.26) even large effects would be; this is a rule of thumb read from
  the seed ranges, not a recorded power calculation.]{#clm-0135 .claim}
- [All 1000 benchmark cases share a single support mask, so generalisation to new supports and the value of occupancy-based
  ideas cannot be tested on this dataset.]{#clm-0136 .claim}
- [Most findings behind this book are preliminary: the null-direction findings were returned for rewording and not re-reviewed,
  and the staged-pilot, spatial-field and simulator-comparison findings have had no confirming independent review.]{#clm-0137 .claim}
- Some numbers in the records are quoted without a registered measurement to check them against, and a few quantities in the
  text are a reviewer's calculation rather than a recorded run; the text says where.
- The book's literature comparisons rest on reading notes; no source has been verified, so there is no bibliography yet.
- All data are noise-free, and the learned results use the same forward model that generated the data.

## Proposed but not done

The following experiments are registered or sketched in the project records; none has produced a result. Their listing
here is a plan, not evidence.

| Proposal | What it would answer | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Supervised, self-supervised, adaptation and identifiability studies on data from an independent simulator (four designs) | Whether supervised and physics-based learning transfer when the training and test forward models differ; whether the priors tested here help on an independent producer | Designed and registered, no data generated, no runs |
| Comparison of image-domain, projection-domain and reconstruction-domain consistency losses | Whether the domain in which consistency is imposed changes the material error | Ready, not run |
| Sensitivity of material accuracy to perturbed spectra, attenuation and geometry | A signed bias for each perturbation against the official model | Proposed with a minimal registration, no runs |
| Network prior study (structural calcification and sum constraints, simple priors, wrong-prior and prior-only controls) | Whether supplying the information a network lacks recovers the split | Proposed, 24 runs planned, gated on the pilot and the owner |
| Acquisition ablation (single-energy, dual-energy and photon counting) with the converged solver under noise | Whether the single-ray ordering of acquisitions survives tomographic coupling and noise | Proposed, not implemented; depends on whether photon counting is in scope |

: Proposed work that has not been done. {#tbl-proposed}

[None of the five proposed studies above, nor a ten-seed replication of the baselines that was deferred, has been run.]{#clm-0138 .claim}
[The pilot also left undone a clipped, away-from-lesion rerun of the high-frequency metric, a longer solve for the
free-calcification arm from a uniform start, and a synthetic lesion-free case that would separate model misspecification from
non-identifiability.]{#clm-0139 .claim} Two engineering items are also blocked: a cross-check of the project's earlier
general attenuation tables against the benchmark's is not well defined, because they share no material except possibly
calcium, and some older planning records have not been tidied.

## Decisions that need human judgement

[The decisions waiting for the project owner are: whether the pilot justifies starting the network-prior study; whether to
approve the pilot's undone runs; whether weak supervision, and how much label information, is acceptable; whether photon
counting is in scope; and whether replication runs and a single evaluation on the test split are worth their cost.]{#clm-0140 .claim}
